questions.q: Where can I get help in my own language?
questions.a: Call the Immigration Contact Center at 1345 or the Danuri helpline at 1577-1366; both offer multiple languages. In Seoul, the Seoul Global Center also offers counseling.

questions.q: What number do I call in an emergency?
questions.a: Call 119 for fire and ambulance and 112 for police. For suicide prevention counseling, call 109.

questions.q: Do I need a residence card?
questions.a: If you will stay more than 90 days, you must register within 90 days of entering Korea. See the Visa guides on this page and check Hi Korea for your situation.

questions.q: My employer hasn't paid my wages. What can I do?
questions.a: Keep a record of your hours and payments, and call the Ministry of Employment and Labor counseling center at 1350. A DHL mentor can listen and help you find the right office. DHL can't give legal advice.

questions.q: Do I need a written contract?
questions.a: Yes, ask for one before you start work, keep a copy, and make sure you understand it. Ask a Korean-speaking friend or mentor to read it with you.

questions.q: How can I start learning Korean for free?
questions.a: Try the KIIP program through Socinet, King Sejong Institute's online courses, and DHL's Survival Korean certificate course.

questions.q: What is TOPIK, and do I need it?
questions.a: TOPIK is the official Korean proficiency test. Universities, employers and some visa types may ask for a TOPIK level, so check the requirements that apply to you.

questions.q: I'm not a Christian. Can I still join DHL?
questions.a: Yes. Everyone is welcome, whatever your background. You can join the community, get practical help, and explore the Bible whenever you're ready.

questions.q: Where should I start reading the Bible?
questions.a: Many people start with the Gospel of John or Mark. DHL's Gospel Class also walks you through the main message step by step.

questions.q: Can I study the Bible in Tagalog or Korean?
questions.a: Yes. Some DHL groups meet in English and Tagalog, and Bible links on this site can open in other translations. Ask to join a Bible study and tell us your language.

questions.q: Which map app works best in Korea?
questions.a: Naver Map and KakaoMap give the most reliable directions for walking, buses and the subway.

questions.q: Where do I see a doctor?
questions.a: For everyday illness, visit a local clinic (의원) and bring your residence card. For emergencies, call 119.

questions.q: How do I throw away trash?
questions.a: Use volume-based trash bags (종량제 봉투) from a convenience store, and separate food waste and recyclables. Rules differ by district.
